messages:
emma: Heads-up — we just got a severity-2 from Support: p99 latency for /v1/generate jumped from ~600ms to ~2.8s for a handful of customers. Support saw it correlate with a config push last night to continuous-batcher defaults. Copying thread here.

raj: ack. which config exactly? batch_size or timeout?

emma: support says they increased continuous_batcher.batch_timeout_ms from 20 -> 100 for several routes to improve throughput. rollout at ~00:15 UTC. Incidents page: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/continuous-batcher?orgId=1&from=now-2h

mike: I see the spike on p99 for routes that hit the batcher. p95 also up but smaller. Looks like tail grows non-linearly when small % of requests wait full timeout and then flush. p99 ~ 2.7s matches 100ms * many sequences? hmm.

sofia: small correction: batch_timeout_ms is 100ms, not seconds. The p99s are in seconds because queuing plus token generation. But yes the long tail looks like requests that missed prefix cache + waited full timeout then got a large batch processed sequentially.

joan: can we reproduce? I can run a synthetic load that mimics 10rps with bursty arrivals and skewed seq lengths.

raj: before repro, can we roll back the config for affected routes to previous timeout? We have a route tag list in the rollout policy.

emma: Support asked to avoid immediate rollback until we confirm mitigation is safe. They want a targeted fix: reduce max_batch_size on those noisy routes or set per-route bypass for low-latency customers.

mike: Repro steps I used locally:
```
# simulate 5 clients, random inter-arrival using poisson
python tools/sim_batcher_load.py --rate 10 --mix "short:0.8,long:0.2" --duration 300 --target /v1/generate
```
Observing p99 jump when batch_timeout_ms=100 and max_batch_size=64.

sofia: logs from runtime: several batches flushed at timeout with sizes 40-60, and KV cache misses. When a timeout flush happens the inference slots get saturated causing queueing behind executing batches.

ops-bot: deploy - success: config/continuous-batcher v2.3 rolled out to prod (tag: cb-timeout-100ms) by ci/cd at 00:15 UTC :white_check_mark:

raj: hypothesis: increasing timeout reduces wasted small batches but increases tail because rare slow-arrival patterns let many requests accumulate and one long decoding run blocks GPU, pushing latency up for those waiting. Tradeoff is batch_size vs timeout.

joan: agree. Another factor: when sequence lengths vary, large-batch execution time grows and blocks smaller requests in same queue because we do per-GPU single-threaded decode.

emma: we need immediate mitigations we can do non-disruptively:
- set per-route max_batch_size lower (eg 32 -> 16) for latency-sensitive customers
- enable prefer-low-latency mode on routes (bypass batching for small requests)
- reduce batch_timeout_ms to 30ms for a canary group
- enable early-flush on token count heuristic
Support prefers targeted per-customer rules.

mike: I can push a rollback of the default timeout to 30ms for the top 10 affected routes as a canary. Will instrument p95/p99 dashboards.

sofia: add a custom circuit-breaker rule: if p99 > 1s for a minute, automatically set route.batcher.bypass=true for that route.

raj: good. Also add metric exported: batch_wait_time_histogram, and label batches by route + batch_size so we can query "count of batches flushed at timeout".

emma: Support provided 3 customer repro payloads. They've been uploaded to /mnt/sre/repro/1781209987/. Joan please run against staging with the config changes.

joan: running now. command:
```
./tools/run_repro.sh /mnt/sre/repro/1781209987/ --config overrides/eng-sre/timeout-canary.json --target staging
```
I'll post generated graphs in 15m.

support-bot: alert: Customer ACME reported increased latency at 01:03 UTC. Ticket #INC-4123 linked.

mike: Canary started: pushed batch_timeout_ms=30 for routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. max_batch_size clipped to 24 for same routes. Watching.

sofia: initial canary metrics: p95 dropped back to ~450ms, p99 to ~630ms for canary hosts. Non-canary still elevated.

raj: good. For long term: we should consider adaptive batch_timeout that shrinks if queue_depth > threshold and grows if throughput low. Also per-route autoregression: if seq_length_variance high -> favor smaller batches.

emma: also want a deployment checklist: when changing batch_timeout, run synthetic with real seq-length distribution, measure "batches_flushed_by_timeout" and "mean_exec_time_by_batch_size".

mike: created PR with rollback + circuit-breaker rule: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge/9872

joan: repro in staging confirms root cause — batcher timeout causing large batches that block GPU. Staging run logs:
```
[2026-03-15 01:10:05] batcher: flushed batch route=/v1/generate size=58 reason=timeout wait_ms=100
[2026-03-15 01:10:05] runtime: start_decode job_id=xyz seq_len=512 est_ms=1200
[2026-03-15 01:10:06] request_queue: depth=20
```

sofia: notes: 1) KV cache hit rate for these routes is low (0.12) so no save there. 2) we should avoid pushing timeout up across the board — targeted throughput improvements may be done by increasing concurrency or enabling prefix cache.

emma: action items summary:
- mike: roll canary -> done (rollback default -> 30ms for named routes) + set max_batch_size clip -> 24 (in progress)
- raj: add circuit-breaker rule + metric labels (infrastructure)
- joan: run full customer repros on staging and attach timelines
- sofia: create runbook blurb for Support to explain tradeoffs and mitigation knobs
- support-bot: keep ticket updated and notify customers impacted

mike: rolled to prod canary hosts, patch id cb-roll-1781209987. I'll keep it pinned for 2 hours and then widen if stable.

support-bot: ticket #INC-4123 updated: canary rollback in progress. Contact: support@redwood.ai

emma: postmortem: once stable, we'll document default batcher profiles and safe value ranges, and add a preflight test for changes to batch_timeout_ms.

raj: long-term follow-ups: adaptive timeout algorithm, per-route SLO tags, and automatic fallback to bypass for latency customers.

sofia: also consider quantization/kv-cache optimizations to shorten decode time for big batches.

joan: final staging graphs attached to the ticket. Canary trending positive. I'll close the repro loop and mark tests green.

mike: thanks everyone. If anyone sees regression after widening canary ping here immediately. :thumbsup:
